pt-porto.varieties: Authorised Douro Demarcated Region varieties (IVDP list), e.g. reds Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz, Tinta Barroca, Tinto Cao, Sousao; whites Malvasia Fina, Gouveio, Viosinho, Rabigato.
pt-porto.min_alcohol: Must at least 11% potential (average). Actual alcohol 16.5-22% depending on category under DL 106/2025 (EU-registered spec: 19-22%, light dry white from 16.5%). Fermentation stopped with grape spirit (aguardente) leaving at least 17.5 g/l sugar.
pt-porto.max_yield: 7,500 kg/ha red and 8,864 kg/ha white grapes for any RDD PDO/PGI wine (750 kg of grapes = 550 l of must), adjustable up to +25% in the annual harvest communique (DL 106/2025, art. 12). The EU-registered 2011 specification still shows 55 hl/ha red and rose, 65 hl/ha white. The amount of fortifying spirit and wine authorised each year is set in the harvest communique.
pt-porto.ageing: IVDP categories: Vintage (single harvest, approved January-June of the 2nd year, bottled by 30 July of the 3rd year, on sale from 1 May of the 2nd year, tasting score 9/10); LBV (single harvest, certified 1 March-31 December of the 4th year, bottled by 31 December of the 6th year); Colheita (single harvest, at least 7 years in wood from 1 September of the 2nd year); Crusted (blend, at least 3 years in bottle); Garrafeira (single harvest, 4-8 years in wood then at least 15 years in glass); Reserva Tawny and Reserva Branco at least 6 years in wood; Reserva Ruby no minimum but quality approval.
pt-porto.styles: Ruby, Tawny, White (Branco), Rose; special categories Reserva, LBV, Vintage, Crusted, Colheita, Garrafeira, age indications.
pt-porto.labelling: Age indications 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 80 anos; VVO (Very Very Old) for wines over 80 years without stated age (80 anos and VVO created January 2025, IVDP Circular 01/2025). Colheita must show harvest and bottling years; Garrafeira shows harvest and final bottling year (Velho over 20 years, Muito Velho over 30). LBV may say Unfiltered, Bottle Matured. 'Port', 'Porto', 'vinho do Porto' and translations protected.
pt-porto.sweetness: Sugar classes: Extra Seco 17.5-40 g/l, Seco 40-65, Meio Seco 65-85, Doce 85-130, Muito Doce or Lagrima over 130 g/l.
pt-porto.other: Storage, bottling, labelling and guarantee seals only inside the Douro Demarcated Region or the Vila Nova de Gaia entreposto; bulk liqueur wines banned in the RDD (DL 106/2025). The 75,000-litre minimum stock to trade Port was abolished in 2025. A Port wine vinegar category was created. Stock top-ups with certified spirit capped at 2% a year (IVDP Circular 05/2026).

pt-madeira.ageing: Canteiro: fortified and aged in wood at least 2 years, never heated, not bottled before 3 years from 1 January after harvest. Frasqueira/Garrafeira: vintage and recommended variety, canteiro, at least 20 years in wood, bottling year shown. Solera: single harvest and variety, at least 5 years in wood, then at most 10% drawn a year.
pt-madeira.styles: Fortified wine by canteiro or estufagem; Rainwater; age-stated, Colheita, Frasqueira, Solera.

pt-madeira.sweetness: Extra seco to doce by Baume (extra seco up to 0.5, doce over 3.5). Varietals tied to sweetness: Sercial seco or extra seco; Verdelho meio seco; Boal meio doce; Malvasias doce; Terrantez meio seco or meio doce. Sweetness term compulsory except on these varietal labels.
pt-madeira.other: Volatile acidity limits 20 meq/l up to 10 years, 25 meq/l to 20 years, 30 meq/l over 20 years. Production rules set by regional Portarias 38-40/2015 (JORAM).
